title: How To Teach Classroom Management On The First Day Of School he-first-day-of-school/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin lays out a detailed sequence for delivering the first-day classroom management lesson with conviction rather than as an unpleasant aside. The steps include privately committing to the plan beforehand, starting the lesson early in the day, making two public promises (to uphold the plan every day and to always treat students with respect), and framing rules and consequences as protecting students' freedom to learn rather than as bad news. He also recommends teaching with visible energy, referencing a posted visual of the rules, giving a full, impassioned review, demonstrating the progression from warning to consequence, modeling misbehavior in a student's shoes, and finishing with an open Q&A so nothing about the plan feels secret or unclear. He closes by contrasting this thorough approach with the ambiguity many students are used to, framing the first day as an opportunity to remove all excuses for future misbehavior.
points: Commit privately to your classroom management plan before students arrive, then make two public promises: to uphold it daily and to always treat students with respect.
Present rules and consequences as protecting students' freedom to learn and enjoy school, not as punitive bad news.
Demonstrate the full progression from an initial warning to a signed consequence letter so students see exactly what will happen.
Model misbehavior yourself, sitting in a student's seat, to make the lesson concrete and memorable.
End with open questions so no part of the plan feels secret, unclear, or difficult to defend.
quotes: No, you must set your feet, narrow your eyes, and teach classroom management in a way your students won’t soon forget.
Before your students arrive, make an ironclad commitment to yourself to abide by the guidelines set forth in your classroom management plan .
To begin your lesson, make a promise to your students that you will uphold your classroom management plan every minute of every day , no exceptions.
Now promise your students that you will always treat them with respect. Promise that you will never yell, scold, or humiliate them in any way.
Your classroom management plan is the very thing that ensures your students’ freedom to learn and enjoy school without interference.

The lesson is most effective if you pretend to be the misbehaving student. Sit at one of their desks and call out without raising your hand, side-talk with a classmate, or engage in any other common misbehavior.
The idea behind teaching classroom management so thoroughly right out of the gate is to remove any and all excuses for poor behavior before they gain a toehold.
